clues: This town is in the Amhara region of Ethiopia. It sits in the Lasta district and the North Wollo Zone.
The dry season here runs from October to March. In those months the weather is best for exploring the temple complex.
Its churches were built between the seventh and thirteenth centuries. They are linked to the reign of a Zagwe king long ago.
Its churches are laid out as a sign of Jerusalem. Their names match that far off holy city too.
Its famed rock cut churches are a World Heritage Site. Pilgrims still come from far away to pray in them.
